runners_data.name: Aura Of Melania
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up filly from Roger Fell whose two runs over 7f have produced mid-pack finishes — the return to 7f is a plus and she handles good going, but no wins or placings in three starts and a modest T14 record (0/12) dampen confidence.|

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.note: Phillip Makin's filly has shown she can finish close (two 2nds in recent form) and handles both good and standard surfaces, making her one of the more interesting hold-up types in the field — wears a hood and Dougie Costello's booking is a positive, though six runs without a win raises the obvious question.|

runners_data.name: Emerald Bay
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — Emerald Bay is actually a P-style runner who won over 8f on good last time, and she steps down in trip here; George Scott's yard is in excellent form (T14: 2/18) and with no rivals to push her in front, this is the obvious tactical base to work from, though the style-fit flag (0.93) notes she is stretching her usual role.|

runners_data.name: Hamdani Mokhater
runners_data.note: James Horton's hold-up type has three runs all on good or good-adjacent ground and has never finished worse than 7th, which at least shows he sees the trip out — 31 days off and no wins or places limit confidence, but Jason Hart's booking is solid and 7f should suit his stamping.|

runners_data.name: Agnes Hathaway
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's filly has run eight times without a win, and her form figures of 8-7-9-6 make for sober reading — her natural position is at the rear, and in a race with this many hold-up types, getting clear daylight in the straight is a real risk; Bell's T14 is strong (2/20) but the horse's form doesn't back it up.|

runners_data.name: Alpaca's Bullet
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's charge carries a "fades in finish" flag and has finished 9th, 7th, and 8th in three runs on good going — all five-furlong starts, so 7f is unproven territory, and the 43-day absence adds uncertainty; a natural closer who has consistently failed to land a blow.|

runners_data.name: Le Grand Etoile
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner also fades in the closing stages according to pace data and has a poor record on good going (1 of 3 sim-going runs placed) — three runs, all in the back half of the field, and Rob Hornby takes over in the saddle; the step up to 7f is a question mark given an unimpressive 6f and 5f record.|

runners_data.name: Magical Life
runners_data.note: J S Moore's hold-up type shows a best of 4th from seven runs, and the headgear (p) worn previously has not unlocked much — Ashley Lewis claims 5lb and the horse's record on standard going is mixed; 12 days since last run is fine, but the overall profile suggests a horse who participates rather than threatens.|

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's gelding is the most interesting hold-up type in the field — a 3rd over 8f on good last time shows stamina and the step back to 7f could sharpen him up; wears a hood, Tom Kiely-Marshall claims 5lb, and four runs all on good going (4/4 sim-going) removes any surface doubt; the 10-day turnaround is a minor query.|

runners_data.name: Postcard
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby's filly ran six days ago (a very quick turnaround) and her form reads 8-9-6-7 — four consecutive poor finishes all on good going, and she wears a hood without obvious improvement; Olivia Tubb claims 5lb but the combination of rapid reappearance and uninspiring form makes this the hardest case to build in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Emerald Bay is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner nursery handicap over 7f at Leicester, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to dictate at a measured, sustainable gallop from the front. The rest of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Agnes Hathaway, Alpaca's Bullet, Le Grand Etoile, Magical Life, Tiger In The Tree, and Postcard are all natural hold-up runners who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are far too many closers for all of them to occupy the rear; in reality, Hamdani Mokhater, Aura Of Melania, and Bluestone Lady are also hold-up operators, meaning the field behind Emerald Bay will be a dense, compressed bunch racing in a confined space. With one horse controlling a steady fractions over a flat 7f, the race is unlikely to produce the sort of searching end-to-end gallop that stretches out closers — instead, it sets up a situation where the horse who can travel best through the pack and produce the sharpest turn of foot in the final two furlongs holds the advantage. This race shape firmly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with tactical speed and the ability to pick through traffic, rather than deep closers who need a hard pace to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Emerald Bay Controls Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Bay is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a steady, uncontested gallop that she can maintain through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Emerald Bay dictates every yard, gets a soft lead at comfortable fractions, and the hold-up pack behind is too far back or too bunched to reel her in before the line; her recent winning run over this going profile and step back up to 7f suit her well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the hold-up runners find clear daylight entering the final two furlongs, enabling a late surge.
scenarios.body: A crawling tempo compresses the field and brings Emerald Bay back to the pack in the closing stages, allowing one or two of the better-credentialed hold-up types to pick her off; horses from midfield who are actually true closers would benefit most if they can find a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking in third or fourth takes a sit just off the modest pace and quickens decisively when the field fans out in the straight.
scenarios.body: With traffic issues likely in the hold-up pack, the horse closest to Emerald Bay who has the tactical awareness to travel smoothly and strike at the right moment earns a decisive positional advantage; Tiger In The Tree's recent 3rd at 8f on good and Hamdani Mokhater's hold-up profile suit this shape best among the redistributed types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Bay fades sharply after leading into the final two furlongs and the race opens up for a rank outsider tracking widest in the straight.
scenarios.body: An unlikely but possible scenario if the leader has been doing too much work in front and weakens abruptly, gifting the race to a fresh-enough runner who manages to avoid the traffic; lower-rated runners with more recent starts could surprise in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Emerald Bay — watch whether she gets a completely uncontested lead or if any runner attempts to press her early; the entire race shape hinges on whether she dictates alone or is harried into a faster pace.

Tiger In The Tree — coming back from a 3rd over 8f on good, he may attempt to sit third or fourth and get the clearest passage of all the hold-up types; watch his position exiting the stalls given the 5lb claim from Kiely-Marshall.

Traffic danger in the straight — with eight genuine or redistributed hold-up runners all trying to find daylight simultaneously in the last 2f, significant bunching is likely; horses drawn widest may get the cleanest run.

Bluestone Lady — the hood and Costello booking suggest connections are expecting a forward move; watch whether she attempts to race closer to the pace than her style suggests, which would give her a material advantage if Emerald Bay fades.

Alpaca's Bullet and Le Grand Etoile — both flagged as "fades in finish" with consistent back-of-field form on good going; if either appears to be travelling well at the two-furlong marker it would be a significant and noteworthy departure from their established profile.
